clue.text: Incapable urban drunk in a dependent state

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the preceding words lurch out of their order

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A helpless city drunk finds himself living in some puppet state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incapable' and 'drunk' look like one description of a sot; one supplies letters and the other stirs them.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana republic is a small, politically unstable country whose economy leans on a single export and on foreign powers.

clue.text: Stone in Riviera affected an ambitious climber

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other word before the mixing
affected here means altered or disturbed, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A social climber putting on airs on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is a social upstart, someone ruthlessly ambitious to rise in status or wealth.

clue.text: Time to open beer with one leading religious convert

indicators.note: to open something you get inside it, so this letter goes within the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: the leading letter is the one at the front of the word that follows

parts.note: one letter taken from the front of this word

explanation.surface: Cracking a beer with a newly converted believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one leading religious' means just one letter, the first, of religious.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to change or modify it, the same as to alter it.

clue.text: In the past, men ate it cooked with bit of oregano

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only a small bit, the first letter, of the herb is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the herb

explanation.surface: Historically, men dined on some dish seasoned with a pinch of oregano.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly, at some earlier period, which is exactly in the past.

clue.text: European in weakened state must eat slice of beef joint

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: something that eats takes another thing inside it

parts.note: being low means feeling weak or run down

indicators.note: a slice is a small portion, here the first letter of the meat

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A frail European must eat some beef to regain strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like more meat after the beef, but it is the body's hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinge joint between the upper arm and forearm.

clue.text: Suggestion: no denture should be flung about the place

indicators.text: should be flung about the place
indicators.note: things flung about land scattered in a new disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tip: don't toss your false teeth around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertone is an underlying hint or implication, a suggestion beneath what is openly said.

clue.text: Member with ring that one bends over backwards for?

definitions.text: that one bends over backwards for?

parts.note: an arm or leg is a member of the body
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Asks which body part with a ring someone would bend over backwards to accommodate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: in the limbo dance one leans backwards to pass under a low bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a Caribbean dance in which performers arch back to shuffle beneath a lowering pole.

clue.text: American behind half of stakes wins a card game

indicators.note: to win something is to take it in, so the pair holds a letter between them

parts.note: can is American slang for the buttocks

indicators.note: only the first half of the next word, three of its six letters, is kept

parts.note: the first half of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American player sitting behind the pot scoops half the stakes at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American behind' reads as a position at the table; it is US slang for a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game, originally from Uruguay, played with two packs.

clue.text: Declare one's commitment to a company in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it would be heard when spoken, not as written

parts.note: a firm is a company

explanation.surface: Pledging loyalty to an employer at a tribunal hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state solemnly or confirm one's support, as when one affirms allegiance.

clue.text: Most eminent duke to welcome Republican leader

indicators.note: a host welcomes a guest in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dukes is old slang for fists, as in 'put up your dukes'

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A top-ranking duke receives the head of the Republican party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duke' wants to be a nobleman; it is boxing slang for a fist.
explanation.definitionFit: First means foremost in rank or importance, the most eminent of all.

clue.text: Old male shoots old lady and northern referee

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
M is the abbreviation for male
buds are young shoots on a plant
one's old lady is one's mother, ma
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A violent tale: an old man guns down an elderly woman and a northern match official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoots' reads as a verb of violence; it is the plural noun for new growth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official who adjudicates complaints between the public and organisations, acting as a neutral arbiter.

clue.text: Where poets might express themselves upside down

definitions.meaning: first meaning, two words: within poetic lines rather than prose
second meaning, one word: turned the other way round

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words; the second keeps it whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Poets write in verse, metrical lines; the single word inverse describes something reversed or turned over.

clue.text: Small deity bitter about experienced warriors

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole string runs back to front

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a god is a deity
a raw wind is a bitterly cold one

explanation.surface: A minor god resentful about seasoned fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' reads as resentful, but here it means piercingly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardogs is a term for veteran soldiers, old campaigners hardened by long service in combat.

clue.text: Problem reversing one car at first in garage?

indicators.note: reversing means running backwards, so the word for a problem is read from its end

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Trouble backing a car out first thing in the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garage' looks like a car's home; it is the dance-music genre, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage is a genre of electronic dance music, so it is an example of music.

clue.text: Character quietly hiding spades, hearts and ace by hand?

definitions.text: Character quietly hiding spades, hearts and ace by hand?

indicators.note: what hides something conceals it inside, so these letters go within the outer pair

parts.note: a card is an eccentric character
S abbreviates spades in card notation
H abbreviates hearts in card notation
A is the abbreviation for ace
R abbreviates right, as in right hand
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A shady figure secretly palming spades, hearts and an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a cheat slipping cards out of sight by sleight of hand. 'by' only joins hand to the list.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a professional cheat at card games who uses tricks such as concealing cards.

clue.text: Female lover soon to meet singer close to Madonna

parts.note: in a mo, short for in a moment, means soon
a singer is slang for an informer, a rat

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the singer's name is kept

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: A girlfriend is soon to meet a vocalist close to the pop star Madonna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' suggests a musician next to Madonna; in criminal slang a singer is someone who sings to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman with whom one is in love, a mistress or sweetheart.

clue.text: Soldier with bow seen on Twitch in a chilly region

parts.note: a soldier is a caste of ant
a bow is curved like an arc
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: An archer spotted on the streaming site Twitch, somewhere freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitch' is capitalised to look like the streaming platform; it is just a nervous spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is the polar region around the South Pole, the coldest area on Earth.

clue.text: A type of model farm vehicle in a big draw?

parts.note: taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A toy tractor in a raffle prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type of model' suggests a scale model; it points to the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractor is something that pulls people in, as a crowd-pulling attraction does.

clue.text: Having gone travelling, I enter hot Eastern countries

indicators.note: letters that have gone travelling wander off and arrive in a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives in sweltering Asian lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is an old-fashioned collective name for the countries of Asia, especially East Asia.

clue.text: Companies of soldiers you must have heard about

indicators.note: something heard is taken by ear, so the word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: troops are soldiers

explanation.surface: Military units you have surely heard tales of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Companies of soldiers' reads as one military phrase; the definition stops at Companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Troupes are companies of performers, such as dancers or actors touring together.

clue.text: Not all sex transports chap with very small part

indicators.note: not all of the next words is used, only a run of letters lying across them

parts.note: letters running from the second letter of the first word

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that not every sex act sends a man with a tiny member into raptures.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a film actor with a walk-on role.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a background performer in a film who has a minimal non-speaking role.

clue.text: Information in a case for constabulary or bureau

indicators.note: one word sits within the others

parts.note: taken as written
gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: a case surrounds its contents, so only the outer letters of the police word are used

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Intelligence on a police matter, whether for the force or a government office.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is an organisation or office providing a service, much like a bureau.

clue.text: Booze too much and deliveries more expensive now

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
prices that are up have risen

explanation.surface: Overdrinking, plus home deliveries costing more these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests the postman; it is cricket, where an over is six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to drink, so oversup means to drink to excess, in an informal coinage.

clue.text: I inspire spy to break into English office at front

indicators.note: breaking into somewhere means getting inside it

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: at front means only the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: the first letter
a rat is a spy or informer

explanation.surface: A first-person boast from an agent who breaks into an English office.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer herself: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Greek Muses, the goddesses who inspire poets, so she can say this.

clue.text: Schematic drawing primarily important for patent

indicators.note: drawing here means drawing in, as one draws on a cigarette, taking something inside

parts.note: a plan is a schematic diagram

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A technical diagram is key when applying for a patent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schematic drawing' reads as a single noun phrase; drawing is the instruction to take something in.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or evident, which is what plain also means.

clue.text: Free publication

definitions.meaning: second meaning: issuing something to the public, such as a press statement or a new record

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words suggest a free newspaper; they are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to liberate; a release is also something issued publicly, like a film or press notice.

clue.text: Get wind and bend over without bit of reticence

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the letter

parts.note: to lean is to bend or incline

indicators.note: only a small bit, the first letter, of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Breaking wind when bending over, without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get wind' wants to mean flatulence; get wind of something means hear about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get wind of something is to find it out, which is one sense of learn, to discover.

clue.text: Be involved or engage in sport on your todd?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to have a role in something

definitions.text: engage in sport on your todd?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: take part in a game on your own

explanation.walkthrough: 'On your todd' is British rhyming slang for alone, from the jockey Tod Sloan; the question mark flags the split reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a part means to contribute or have a role; play apart would be to compete separately.

clue.text: A jerk screening Troy and Room at the Top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a screen hides what is behind it, so these words surround a letter

parts.note: a tic is a sudden jerk or spasm
T is the abbreviation for troy, the system of weights

explanation.surface: An idiot watching the film Troy and the novel Room at the Top.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitals disguise the words: Troy is troy weight, and Room at the Top is the novel's title but means a top-floor room.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room just under the roof, at the top of a house.

clue.text: Flying pest perching on one with many branches?

indicators.note: things flying scatter through the air and land in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An airborne insect alights on a tree with lots of boughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' suggests a tree; it means chain-store outlets, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping centre houses outlets of many retail chains, each one a branch of a larger company.
